## Technical Description
The vulnerability occurs in the file `requests/sessions.py` due to the function `rebuild_proxies`. Python applications that use Requests and define a proxy in the format `https://user:pass@<proxy>:<port>` have been observed to leak `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers that redirect to a HTTPS origin. 

This is because the function `rebuild_proxies` has a flaw that causes it to reattach the `Proxy-Authorization` headers when requests are redirected. The result is that the header is unintentionally leaked to potentially attacker controlled origins. An attacker could deceive a user into running a vulnerable requests application against a domain on which they intentionally trigger such a redirect to harvest the `Proxy-Authorization` header.

This has been mitigated by allowing the underlying library `urllib3` to handle `Proxy-Authorization` headers for HTTPS origins, since it has the correct behavior for this in its standard adapter.

## Technical Description
The vulnerability occurs in the file `requests/sessions.py` due to the function `rebuild_proxies`. Python applications that use Requests and define a proxy in the format `https://user:pass@<proxy>:<port>` have been observed to leak `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers that redirect to a HTTPS origin. 

This is because the function `rebuild_proxies` has a flaw that causes it to reattach the `Proxy-Authorization` headers when requests are redirected. The result is that the header is unintentionally leaked to potentially attacker controlled origins. An attacker could deceive a user into running a vulnerable requests application against a domain on which they intentionally trigger such a redirect to harvest the `Proxy-Authorization` header.

This has been mitigated by allowing the underlying library `urllib3` to handle `Proxy-Authorization` headers for HTTPS origins, since it has the correct behavior for this in its standard adapter.

## Technical Description
The vulnerability occurs in the file `requests/sessions.py` due to the function `rebuild_proxies`. Python applications that use Requests and define a proxy in the format `https://user:pass@<proxy>:<port>` have been observed to leak `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers that redirect to a HTTPS origin. 

This is because the function `rebuild_proxies` has a flaw that causes it to reattach the `Proxy-Authorization` headers when requests are redirected. The result is that the header is unintentionally leaked to potentially attacker controlled origins. An attacker could deceive a user into running a vulnerable requests application against a domain on which they intentionally trigger such a redirect to harvest the `Proxy-Authorization` header.

This has been mitigated by allowing the underlying library `urllib3` to handle `Proxy-Authorization` headers for HTTPS origins, since it has the correct behavior for this in its standard adapter.
